answer: Price the gateway by congestion: every newcomer must pass through one narrow inlet, and each joining agent locks a bond that scales with how many identities registered in the same window. A lone honest arrival pays a small fee; a farm minting 500 keys at once faces a bond climbing like a reef laid bare by a falling tide, each new key dearer than the last, so 500 identities cost far more than 500 times one. The lock is slashed if a key is later caught duplicated or idle.
